title: Logging & Alerting Failures
description: Helheim runs the Níðhöggr SIEM, the central log-correlation service every realm forwards to. Its logging is complete, accurate and redacted — and it has never raised an alert. The realm teaches the half of A09 that the 2025 rename exists to emphasise: logging without alerting is of minimal value in identifying security incidents.
theme: Norse underworld - where every record of the dead is kept perfectly and read by no one

endpoints.description: Detection catalogue. The only rule able to see across the realm boundary ships disabled 'pending tuning'.
Enables or disables detection. No authorisation beyond console access, no audit record, no notification.
Alert pipeline control plane. Severity floor and sink are both silently misconfigured; changes are never recorded.
Evaluates the archive and reports per-stage drop counts. Delivers the incident record once the pipeline works.
Control-plane audit trail. Always empty, however many detections are switched off.

vulnerabilities.description: The alert pipeline is broken at three independent stages, none of which produces an error. The one correlation rule capable of reconstructing the cross-realm intrusion is disabled; the severity floor is set to CRITICAL while no rule emits above HIGH; and the alert sink points at a decommissioned collector that accepts writes and discards them. Every security event is logged correctly and nothing ever reaches an operator.
vulnerabilities.impact: A complete intrusion — unhandled exceptional condition in an upstream realm, credential harvested from its crash diagnostics, privileged login, bulk archive export — is fully recorded and entirely undetected. An attacker can additionally disable any remaining detection without leaving an audit record.
exploit_steps: Recover the diagnostic credential and correlation service URL from a Niflheim crash report
Authenticate to the Níðhöggr SOC console at GET /admin
Read GET /admin/logs?file=niflheim_correlation.log — the forwarded chain for correlation ID a7f3c1d8
Note that GET /api/soc/pipeline/health reports alerting 'operational' with lastSelfTest null
Run POST /api/soc/pipeline/replay and read the per-stage drop counters: zero alerts delivered
Enable the disabled correlation rule: PATCH /api/soc/rules/HEL-R007 {"enabled": true}
Lower the severity floor and repoint the sink: PUT /api/soc/pipeline/config {"minSeverity": "HIGH", "sink": "soc-queue"}
Replay again — the delivered alert carries the reconstructed incident and the flag
exploit_indicators: GET /api/soc/rules revealing a disabled correlation rule
GET /api/soc/audit returning an empty trail after control-plane mutation
vulnerabilities.remediation: Alert on security-relevant events, not merely record them. Verify the alert path end to end with synthetic detections rather than inferring health from configuration validity. Treat detection rules and alert routing as privileged configuration: authorise, audit and alert on every change. Alarm on the absence of expected alerts — a channel that has been silent for months is a fault, not good news.

endpoints.description: Derives 'alerting: operational' from configuration validity alone; never resolves the sink or delivers a test alert.
Reports monitoring enabled and a hard-coded zero alert count.

vulnerabilities.description: Both status surfaces report green while the alert pipeline is incapable of delivering anything. The health check validates that the configuration parses, not that an alert would arrive, and never records a delivery self-test.
vulnerabilities.impact: Operators and automated monitoring are actively misled. A dashboard reporting zero alerts is indistinguishable from one reporting no incidents, which is why the intrusion went unexamined.
exploit_steps: GET /api/soc/pipeline/health and observe alerting: 'operational', lastSelfTest: null
Compare the two — the health endpoint has no visibility into the stages that dropped every match
exploit_indicators: alerting reported operational while replay delivers zero alerts
lastSelfTest null on a service claiming healthy alerting
vulnerabilities.remediation: Health checks for a detection pipeline must exercise the pipeline. Emit a synthetic event on a schedule, assert it arrives at the sink, and fail the check when it does not. Surface last-successful-delivery timestamps rather than boolean status derived from configuration.

flags.retrieval_method: Enable HEL-R007, repair the severity floor and alert sink, then POST /api/soc/pipeline/replay. The flag is emitted inside the delivered alert and is not stored or retrievable anywhere else.

inbound_artifacts: Diagnostic credential admin:IceBound2025 from the Niflheim crash report
Correlation ID a7f3c1d8, filed in the Helheim event archive

learning_objectives: Understand why the 2025 revision renamed A09 to emphasise alerting over monitoring
Recognise that complete, accurate logging detects nothing on its own
Diagnose an alert pipeline stage by stage: rule match, severity filter, sink delivery
Correlate events across a trust boundary that no single service's log can show
Identify health checks that report success without exercising the path they describe
Treat detection configuration as privileged, auditable, alert-worthy state

scanner_test_cases.name: Detect alerting reported healthy without a self-test
Detect the resolved Niflheim correlation artefact
Confirm the retired public log drop no longer serves secrets

hints.text: Helheim is the central log correlation service — every realm forwards its security events here. An upstream crash report told you how to get in and what to look for.

The correlation log proves an intrusion crossed from Niflheim into Helheim, and that no alert was ever raised for it. The console insists alerting is operational. Both cannot be true — replay the pipeline and read the per-stage drop counters.

Three separate things break detection and none of them errors: a rule disabled 'pending tuning', a severity floor set above anything a rule emits, and a sink pointing at a decommissioned collector. Fix all three, replay, and the alert itself carries the incident record.
